status: Data drop 3 of the geometric LOD study, after the 2026-10-31 review (BEMGen stage LOD1, D-219 to D-224): schema 1.2.0 lists every planned zoning, those the generator refused (status Invalid) with their reason; a recommendation is bounded by the reference's zone count, so the full-service restaurant 4A cells, where only a finer zoning meets the threshold, have none and are flagged finer_than_reference (D-220; R3: 214 of 264 cells with a recommendation); deduplication keeps the both-on twin (D-221); the cost medians drop duplicate twins and weight the timed prototypes equally (D-222); the files state the unjudged loads and a threshold sensitivity (D-223); and R4's small-hotel cells were run again under BEMGen's heat-transfer rule (D-211), so no zoning of the sub-study fails (D-224). The R5 repeat check is archived as published and cannot be re-derived (D-219). Nothing is pending.

study.name: lod-study-v1
study.title: How Much Thermal Zoning Detail Is Enough?
study.design: Each test case is one DOE/PNNL prototype building generated by BEMGen's DOE generator at the prototype's own dimensions, with the prototype's atlas programs (deterministic ruleset schedules), the atlas 90.1 unified construction set of its vintage and climate zone, and the pinned TMY3 weather of the zone's representative city. The reference site is the prototype's full zoning (NoSimplification + Stack, IWHT and FHT on); the test sites are the zoning simplifications with geometry, programs, envelope and weather fixed. Ideal-loads sensible heating and cooling are the primary outputs; HVAC and service hot water are excluded.
